title: Ezekiel Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The hand of the Lord GOD falls upon Ezekiel
The image of jealousy at the north gate
Ezekiel is lifted up to Jerusalem
The elders of Judah sit before Ezekiel
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the Lord GOD falls upon Ezekiel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:1 states that the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon Ezekiel as he sat in his house with the elders of Judah, making this the first event mentioned.

questions.question: What appearance did Ezekiel behold in Ezekiel 8:2?
options: A likeness as the appearance of fire
A bright star in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: A likeness as the appearance of fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:2 describes that Ezekiel beheld a likeness as the appearance of fire.

questions.question: How is the fire described in Ezekiel 8:2?
options: From the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, brightness like amber
questions.correctAnswer: From the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, brightness like amber
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:2 specifies the fire as being from his loins downwards and brightness like amber from his loins upwards.

questions.question: What did the form of a hand do in Ezekiel 8:3?
options: Took Ezekiel by a lock of his head
questions.correctAnswer: Took Ezekiel by a lock of his head
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:3 states that the form of a hand took Ezekiel by a lock of his head.

questions.question: Where was Ezekiel brought in the visions of God according to Ezekiel 8:3?
options: To Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north
To the city gate facing south
questions.correctAnswer: To Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:3 indicates that Ezekiel was brought to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate toward the north.

questions.question: What was at the door of the inner gate according to Ezekiel 8:3?
options: The seat of the image of jealousy
questions.correctAnswer: The seat of the image of jealousy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:3 states there was the seat of the image of jealousy which provoketh to jealousy.

questions.question: What did Ezekiel see according to Ezekiel 8:4?
options: The glory of the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of the God of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:4 mentions the glory of the God of Israel was there as in the vision seen in the plain.

questions.question: What command did the voice give Ezekiel in Ezekiel 8:5?
options: Lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north
Go stand at the temple gate
Write the vision on a scroll
Tell the elders of Judah to repent
questions.correctAnswer: Lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:5 records the command to lift up his eyes toward the north.

questions.question: Where was the image of jealousy located according to Ezekiel 8:5?
options: Northward at the gate of the altar in the entry
At the south gate of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Northward at the gate of the altar in the entry
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:5 states the image of jealousy was northward at the gate of the altar in the entry.

questions.question: What did the Lord ask Ezekiel in Ezekiel 8:6?
options: Seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here?
Will you speak to the elders of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:6 quotes the Lord asking Ezekiel if he sees the great abominations committed by Israel.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 8:6, why should the Lord go far off from his sanctuary?
options: Because of the great abominations the house of Israel committeth
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the great abominations the house of Israel committeth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:6 explains the Lord would go far off from his sanctuary due to the great abominations committed.

questions.question: What did the Lord tell Ezekiel to do after seeing the first abominations in Ezekiel 8:6?
options: Turn yet again to see greater abominations
questions.correctAnswer: Turn yet again to see greater abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:6 instructs Ezekiel to turn again to see even greater abominations.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel saw the glory of the God of Israel at the door of the inner gate in the vision.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:4 says the glory of the God of Israel was there according to the vision.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of Judah were sitting before Ezekiel when the hand of the Lord fell upon him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:1 states the elders of Judah sat before Ezekiel when the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon him.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was brought to the Mount of Olives in the vision.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:3 says he was brought to Jerusalem to the door of the inner gate toward the north, not to the Mount of Olives.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Ezekiel see when he looked at the hole in the wall?
questions.correctAnswer: A door
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw a door after he dug in the wall, as stated in Ezekiel 8:8.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 8:9 promise will happen if someone goes in as commanded in Ezekiel 8:8?
options: They will see the glory of God
questions.correctAnswer: They will behold wicked abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:9 states that upon entering, he will see the wicked abominations being committed.

questions.question: What did Ezekiel see on the walls when he entered?
options: Idols of the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Idols of the house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:10 describes seeing every form of creeping things and idols portrayed on the wall.

questions.question: What did the ancients of Israel do before the idols?
questions.correctAnswer: Burned incense
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:11 mentions that each man had his censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense went up.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 8:12 reveal about the thoughts of the ancients regarding God's presence?
options: They believed God was watching them
They thought God had forsaken the earth
They were fearful of God's judgment
They felt secure in their actions
questions.correctAnswer: They thought God had forsaken the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:12 reveals that they believed the LORD did not see them and had forsaken the earth.

questions.question: What should be the response of a believer upon witnessing wickedness as described in Ezekiel 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and pray
questions.explanation: Believers are called to respond to wickedness with repentance and prayer, aligning with a call for holiness and integrity.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel's vision challenge the complacency of the people?
questions.correctAnswer: By revealing their secret sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's vision exposes the hidden abominations, challenging the people's belief that they could hide from God's view.

questions.question: In what way does Ezekiel's experience demonstrate the consequences of idolatry?
options: It results in judgment and removal from God’s presence
questions.correctAnswer: It results in judgment and removal from God’s presence
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates that the abominations lead to God's judgment and a distancing from His sanctuary.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel's encounter teach about the nature of God's awareness of sin?
options: God is unaware of our sins
God sees all actions done in secret
questions.correctAnswer: God sees all actions done in secret
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:12 highlights that the ancients believed the LORD could not see them, yet God is fully aware of all actions.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'image of jealousy' mentioned in Ezekiel 8?
options: It represents God's anger towards idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God's anger towards idolatry
questions.explanation: The 'image of jealousy' represents God's rightful anger and the provocation caused by idolatry, as seen in Ezekiel 8:3.

questions.question: What role did the elders of Judah play in Ezekiel's vision?
options: They were engaged in idolatrous practices
questions.correctAnswer: They were engaged in idolatrous practices
questions.explanation: The elders are seen participating in abominations, demonstrating the spiritual decline among the leaders of Israel.

questions.question: What is the main theme of Ezekiel 8 regarding the relationship between God and His people?
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment due to unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes the consequences of unfaithfulness and the seriousness of idolatry leading to judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was brought to witness the abominations committed by the house of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was indeed brought to witness the abominations, as stated in Ezekiel 8:9.

questions.question: True or False: The vision Ezekiel experienced was meant to show God's approval of the people's actions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The vision highlighted the wickedness and abominations, showing God's disapproval and the need for repentance.

questions.question: True or False: The elders were unaware of their sins during the vision.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The ancients believed they were unseen by God, but the vision revealed their awareness of their actions, as per Ezekiel 8:12.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 8:14, what were the women doing at the door of the gate of the LORD's house toward the north?
questions.correctAnswer: Weeping for Tammuz
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:14 explicitly describes women sitting and weeping for Tammuz at the door of the gate of the LORD's house toward the north.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 8:16, how were the men positioned when worshipping, and what were they worshipping?
options: Facing the temple, worshipping the LORD
With backs toward the temple, worshipping the sun toward the east
Kneeling before the altar, worshipping Baal
questions.correctAnswer: With backs toward the temple, worshipping the sun toward the east
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:16 describes about twenty-five men with their backs toward the temple of the LORD and faces toward the east, worshipping the sun toward the east.

questions.question: What reason does Ezekiel 8:17 give for God's anger toward the house of Judah?
options: They built altars to foreign gods
They filled the land with violence and provoked God to anger
questions.correctAnswer: They filled the land with violence and provoked God to anger
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:17 states that the house of Judah committed abominations, filled the land with violence, and returned to provoke God to anger.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 8:18, how does God declare He will respond to the abominations and cries of the people?
options: He will forgive them if they repent
His eye shall not spare, and He will not hear their cries
He will send prophets to warn them
questions.correctAnswer: His eye shall not spare, and He will not hear their cries
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:18 explains that God will deal in fury, not spare His eye, have no pity, and will not hear their loud cries.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 8:13, what does God command the prophet to do?
options: Turn again to see greater abominations
Pray for the people of Jerusalem
Go forth and gather the elders
questions.correctAnswer: Turn again to see greater abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:13 commands the prophet to turn again and see greater abominations that they do.

questions.question: What action is described in Ezekiel 8:17 by the phrase 'they put the branch to their nose'?
options: A ritual to smell incense pleasing to God
An idolatrous practice symbolizing their abominations
A purification rite performed by priests
A sign of mourning for the temple
questions.correctAnswer: An idolatrous practice symbolizing their abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:17 mentions 'they put the branch to their nose' as part of their abominations, indicating a detestable idolatrous practice provoking God’s anger.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Tammuz' refer to in Ezekiel 8:14?
options: A Babylonian deity associated with fertility and seasonal cycles
A type of incense used in worship
questions.correctAnswer: A Babylonian deity associated with fertility and seasonal cycles
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Tammuz' in Ezekiel 8:14 refers to a Babylonian god of fertility and seasonal death and resurrection cycles, whose worship was condemned as idolatry.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in Ezekiel 8:13-16, where the prophet is shown increasingly greater abominations?
questions.correctAnswer: Progressive intensification
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:13-16 employs progressive intensification, where the prophet is repeatedly told to turn again to see greater abominations, emphasizing the increasing severity of the sins.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s judgment on idolatry and abominations seen in Ezekiel 8:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:18-21
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18-21 discusses God's wrath against ungodliness and unrighteousness, echoing the judgment pronounced in Ezekiel 8:18 on abominations and idolatry.

questions.question: Ezekiel 8:4 describes the 'glory of the God of Israel.' Which Old Testament passage similarly describes God's glory departing from the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 10:18-19
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 10:18-19 describes the glory of the LORD departing from the temple, connecting with Ezekiel 8:4's vision of God's glory at the temple as a context for judgment.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the vision of the women weeping for Tammuz in Ezekiel 8:14?
options: The prophet is shown idols painted on the wall
The prophet is commanded to dig in the wall
The prophet is brought to the door of the gate of the LORD's house toward the north
The prophet is told to prophesy against Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet is brought to the door of the gate of the LORD's house toward the north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:14 is immediately preceded by the command to turn again and see greater abominations and the bringing of the prophet to the door of the gate of the LORD's house toward the north, as described in Ezekiel 8:13.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the cultural context of the 'women weeping for Tammuz' in Ezekiel 8:14?
options: A Jewish mourning ritual for the dead
A pagan fertility cult practice adopted from Babylonian religion
A prophetic lament for the destruction of Jerusalem
A symbolic act of repentance before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: A pagan fertility cult practice adopted from Babylonian religion
questions.explanation: The weeping for Tammuz in Ezekiel 8:14 is a pagan fertility cult practice originating from Babylonian religion, condemned as idolatrous in the Hebrew Bible.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 8:12 reveal the mentality of the elders of Israel while committing abominations?
options: They believed the LORD was watching and would punish them
They claimed that the LORD did not see and had forsaken the earth
They sought to please the LORD by secret worship
They were afraid but compelled by tradition
questions.correctAnswer: They claimed that the LORD did not see and had forsaken the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:12 states the elders said, 'The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth,' revealing their false belief that God was unaware or indifferent to their abominations.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the symbolic meaning of the 'image of jealousy' mentioned in Ezekiel 8:3,5?
options: A representation of God's wrath against idolatry
An idol provoking God's jealousy due to Israel's unfaithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: An idol provoking God's jealousy due to Israel's unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The 'image of jealousy' in Ezekiel 8:3 and 8:5 symbolizes an idol provoking God's jealousy because of Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness, causing Him to withdraw His presence.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'thick cloud of incense' in the vision of Ezekiel 8:11?
options: It symbolizes prayers ascending to God
It represents the prevalence of idolatrous worship before God
It is a sign of purification and holiness
It indicates the presence of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the prevalence of idolatrous worship before God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:11 shows seventy elders with censers and a thick cloud of incense, symbolizing widespread idolatrous worship, which provokes God's judgment.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 8:2 teach about the nature of God's presence?
options: God's presence is radiant and consuming like fire
God appears only in human form
God's presence is silent and invisible
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence is radiant and consuming like fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:2 describes the appearance of God's presence as fire and brightness, indicating the consuming holiness and radiant glory of God.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness does Ezekiel 8:6 reveal?
options: Sin provokes God to distance Himself from His sanctuary
Sin can be hidden from God's sight
Sin is only a private matter without communal consequences
Sin is primarily ignorance rather than rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: Sin provokes God to distance Himself from His sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:6 states that the abominations committed by Israel cause God to go far off from His sanctuary, showing the serious relational breach sin causes between God and His people.

questions.question: What doctrine about idolatry is taught in Ezekiel 8:10?
options: Idolatry includes representations of abominable beasts and creeping things
Idolatry is only a matter of foreign gods
Idolatry is permitted if done in secret
Idolatry is a minor offense compared to other sins
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry includes representations of abominable beasts and creeping things
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:10 shows that idolatry in Israel included images of creeping things and abominable beasts, broadening the understanding of idolatry as corrupt worship involving false images.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 8:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:4 notes the presence of the glory of God, indicating His holiness and the pure, glorious nature of His presence among His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly evident in Ezekiel 8:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:18 emphasizes God's fury and refusal to spare or pity the sinful, demonstrating His attribute of righteous judgment against persistent rebellion.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 8 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's judgment on idolatry?
options: It serves as a prophetic warning similar to the destruction of Jerusalem in 2 Kings
It encourages idolatry as a cultural practice
It shows God's indifference to idolatry
It denies that idolatry provokes God's anger
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a prophetic warning similar to the destruction of Jerusalem in 2 Kings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8's depiction of abominations and God's judgment prepares the way for the destruction of Jerusalem described in historical books like 2 Kings, showing a consistent biblical theme of judgment for idolatry.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 8:16 make regarding worship?
options: It contrasts true worship of God with pagan sun worship
It endorses sun worship as acceptable
It ignores the problem of false worship
It presents worship as irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts true worship of God with pagan sun worship
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:16 shows men worshipping the sun, highlighting idolatry's contrast with true worship of Yahweh, a key theme throughout redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 8:11 and Ezekiel 8:12 teach about human sin and divine perception?
options: Human sin is often hidden but not hidden from God's sight
God does not perceive secret sin
Sin committed in secret is excusable
God only sees public sins, not private ones
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin is often hidden but not hidden from God's sight
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:11-12 describe elders committing abominations in secret, yet God sees all, refuting the sinful claim that 'The LORD seeth us not.'

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine judgment and human rebellion is taught by Ezekiel 8:17 and 8:18 together?
options: Persistent sin provokes God's anger leading to irreversible judgment
God's judgment is always delayed indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent sin provokes God's anger leading to irreversible judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 8:17-18 emphasize that the house of Judah's violence and abominations provoke God’s anger and result in His fierce judgment without pity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 8:14 and Ezekiel 8:15 teach about syncretism and false worship?
options: Syncretism with pagan deities like Tammuz is a grievous abomination to God
Pagan mourning rituals are acceptable in Israel
False worship is tolerated if performed by women
Worshiping foreign gods does not affect Israel's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Syncretism with pagan deities like Tammuz is a grievous abomination to God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:14-15 depict women weeping for Tammuz, a pagan deity, highlighting the seriousness of syncretistic worship as a greater abomination.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 8:7-13 is merely dramatic storytelling with no real theological import. What does Ezekiel 8:7-13 actually teach about Israel's spiritual condition?
options: It reveals the secret and institutionalized nature of Israel's idolatry
It shows Israel was fully faithful in private worship
It denies that idolatry was widespread
It suggests God condones human inventions in worship
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the secret and institutionalized nature of Israel's idolatry
questions.explanation: Verses 7-13 expose the secret chambers where elders commit idolatry with censers, showing the depth and official nature of the spiritual corruption.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's guidance and revelation is taught in Ezekiel 8:3?
options: God actively reveals spiritual realities through visions
God remains silent and hidden from human perception
God only reveals Himself through natural phenomena
God's guidance is limited to written scripture
questions.correctAnswer: God actively reveals spiritual realities through visions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:3 depicts God lifting Ezekiel in visions to Jerusalem to reveal spiritual abominations, demonstrating God's active revelatory work.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 8:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Jealousy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:5 mentions the 'image of jealousy' and God's focus toward the north gate, emphasizing His attribute of jealousy for His holiness and covenant.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from the presence of 'seventy men of the ancients' in Ezekiel 8:11?
options: Leadership was complicit in idolatry, indicating corporate sin
Only the common people sinned, not leaders
Idolatry was limited to one isolated group
The elders were unaware of the sins being committed
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership was complicit in idolatry, indicating corporate sin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 8:11 shows elders participating in idolatrous incense worship, highlighting that sin permeated Israel’s leadership, not just individuals.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 8:9 and Ezekiel 8:10 teach about the nature of idolatrous sins?
options: Idolatry involves both imagery and worship of abominable creatures
Idolatry is purely spiritual with no physical representation
Idolatry is confined to foreign nations
Idolatry is only verbal and not acted upon
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry involves both imagery and worship of abominable creatures
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 describe a hidden room full of images of creeping things and abominable beasts, illustrating the tangible and visual nature of idolatry.
